title: Timescape supernova evidence depends on likelihood conditioning and selection

source_evidence.locator: Secs.2-4, Eqs.(1)-(5), Table1, Figs.1-3, PDF pp2-6

assumptions: Author method fixes SALT2 stretch and colour at the event estimates and retains a Gaussian common-magnitude population with intrinsic variance. This replaces the earlier population model with different conditioning.
Pantheon+ light-curve rows, calibration/systematic covariance, CMB-frame transformation, low-redshift selection, proper prior measure and fixed distance normalization jointly define the comparison.
Flat LambdaCDM is the comparison model; timescape retains its own wall-observer averaged geometry. Reusing observations and covariance from Lane et al. is not independent confirmation.
predictions: Authors report ln(Z_TS/Z_flat-LambdaCDM)>5 for their full P+1690 sample and >1 for z_min>=0.075; these are conditioned evidence results, not a measurement of timescape or general model independence.
The reported preference and nuisance estimates change with cuts and the revised conditioning; a paired same-event audit can test the sensitivity without pooling overlapping subsamples.
A model-shared dimension-only normalization error cancels in a Bayes ratio at fixed selected rows; selection, covariance or parameter-prior differences need separate checks.
